review_comment: The DeviceListView uses URL parameters directly to query 2FA devices without verifying the requesting user's authorization. This allows potential unauthorized access to view other users' 2FA device information. Unlike DeviceUpdateView which properly uses self.request.user for authorization, this view bypasses access controls. Add authorization verification to ensure the requesting user has permission to view the target user's devices before querying TOTPDevice.objects.devices_for_user().

The DeviceDeleteView uses POST-supplied user_id for redirect instead of the authenticated user's ID, unlike other views that correctly use self.request.user.id. This creates a potential authorization bypass where users could be redirected to view other users' 2FA device lists. Use self.request.user.id instead of POST data to ensure users can only access their own device management pages.

DeviceDeleteView performs direct database lookup using URL parameters without verifying the requesting user owns the target TOTPDevice. Unlike DeviceUpdateView which properly scopes queries to the current user's devices, this endpoint could allow unauthorized device deletion. Modify get_queryset to use devices_for_user(self.request.user) with proper filtering to ensure users can only delete their own devices.

The patch adds a hidden user_id field that flows into redirect URL construction without validation. While this creates a tamperable parameter, CWE-863 requires demonstration of an incorrect authorization check, not just missing validation. To address the validation issue, verify the user_id parameter matches the authenticated user's permissions before using it in the redirect URL, or derive it from server-side session state instead of client-supplied data.
